rationale: Both candidates miss linyueqian's cumulative/delta re-slice bug and the audio_tokenizer_v2.py:949 ceil/floor padding bug, but Y covers both of the two High-severity ground-truth findings substantively (the stream-slot leak, explained with a deeper id-space mechanism, and the legacy-checkpoint-parses-as-v2 codec issue matching hsliuustc's report almost exactly), while X only surfaces the v2-codec issue as a buried 'minor' aside and frames the slot leak as mostly already resolved. Several findings converge independently between X and Y (max_new_frames TypeError at talker.py:1462, WER PCM fallback quality bug, NPU seq_token_counts gap), which is strong evidence both are grounded rather than fabricated, keeping precision comparable; X edges out slightly on directly diff-verifiable findings (the unconditional tts_local_seed write) and literal suggestion blocks. Both give concrete file/line findings with proposed fixes, but Y's broader and better-prioritized coverage of the real high-severity issues gives it the edge.
